Tsamai (also known as Ts'amay, S'amai, Tamaha, Tsamako, Tsamakko, Bago S'amakk-Ulo) is an Afroasiatic language spoken in Ethiopia. [1] Tsamai is a member of the Dullay dialect continuum. Tsamai, also known as Ts'amakko, is classified as a Lowland East Cushitic language within the Afroasiatic phylum, specifically belonging to the Dullay subgroup or dialect continuum. Tsamai is a stable indigenous language of Ethiopia. It belongs to the Afro-Asiatic language family. The language is used as a first language by all in the ethnic community. It is not known to be taught in schools.
